details: Malicious package. `@iky-erza/baileys` is a trojanized fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library (@whiskeysockets/baileys). `makeNewsletterSocket` in `lib/Socket/newsletter.js` holds a hidden list of channel identifiers (stored as a base64-looking string, `0029Vb9EQN59RZAWWZpeek3X=`, which is in fact a WhatsApp channel invite code) and sets a timer that, 150 seconds after every socket is created, base64-decodes each entry and issues a newsletter FOLLOW for it from the victim account. There is no option to disable this and the README does not mention it. As published, the decode step mangles the invite code, so the follow request targets an invalid identifier; the concealed auto-follow logic is nonetheless present and runs on every connection. `lib/Socket/luxu.js`, which `messages-send.js` uses for event messages, stamps them with forwarded-newsletter context naming channel "PouCode" (120363421563597486@newsletter); poll-result messages default their newsletter name to 120363399602691477@newsletter unless the caller supplies one. The same channel JIDs appear in other trojanized Baileys forks in this campaign. Legitimate Baileys never hardcodes a channel or auto-follows one. Version 0.1.0 carries this code; the `0.0.0-stage` placeholder does not.
